correctness.rationale: Every distinct coset is included once, so each coset normal term is a right-subgroup sum. A unitary n-point Fourier transform on rotation and reflection indices decomposes all \(2n\) coordinates into the constant 2-by-2 block and 2-by-2 nonzero-frequency blocks. Their exact eigenvalues give nullity \(\gcd(a,n)-1\) without numerical extrapolation and fix the extremal eigenvalues. For positive weights the largest eigenvalue is \(n\alpha+2(\beta+\gamma)\) and the smallest is \(\min\{n\alpha,\beta+\gamma-R\}\); optimization first in \(n\alpha\) then \(\beta\gamma\) at fixed sum proves the unique sharp weight ratios. The actual coset-matrix checker passed 648 exact modular-rank tests, 858 numerical full-spectrum tests, 84 subfamily tests, and 189 weighting comparisons; tests are corroborative, not universal proof. Boundaries \(n\ge3\) and \(1\le a<n\) are explicit.

value.rationale: Restricted dihedral finite-group tomography has a natural minimal-direction question: exactly three complete maximal-cyclic families suffice if and only if the two reflection generators span all rotations, and otherwise an exact arithmetic nullity quantifies the loss. The formula also yields complete singular values and a sharp unique acquisition design that reduces condition-number growth from \(n^{3/2}\) to \(n\). These are motivated structural/inverse-problem facts across an infinite natural family, not only a finite example or minor constant improvement.
